metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent encountered Access Denied on drugs.com. Tried Google search (got SSL error), alternative URLs (npg.nature.com - also blocked), then opened terminal and used curl to fetch content from Wikipedia, NIAID, nature.com, and KEGG over 50 turns. Never reached drugs.com/npc/ or /npp/.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can click Chrome address bar, type URLs, perform Google search attempts, open terminal, run curl/bash commands, navigate between windows
metadata.failure_analysis: drugs.com blocked VM IP (Access Denied). Google.com had SSL certificate error in browser. External websites largely inaccessible in this VM environment.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to navigating to Chrome internal history page (chrome://history) which requires no network access. Model demonstrated ability to type URLs in address bar.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to chrome://history. Evaluator uses is_expected_url_pattern_match to check the active tab URL matches the chrome://history pattern. [Fixed: added goto_prefix='' to result config to prevent default 'https://' prefix on chrome:// internal URL]
fix_history: Fix 1: Added 'goto_prefix': '' to active_url_from_accessTree result config to prevent prepending 'https://' to chrome:// internal URLs, which caused the pattern 'chrome://history.*' to never match.

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction requires opening Chrome's browsing history page (chrome://history). The evaluator correctly verifies this single requirement.

Getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' is configured with 'goto_prefix': '' which prevents the default 'https://' prefix from being prepended. This correctly handles chrome:// internal URLs, returning the raw address bar text (e.g., 'chrome://history').

Metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' receives rules={'expected': ['chrome://history.*']} after framework unwraps the rule type. It uses re.search to match the pattern against the getter result, which correctly matches 'chrome://history' or 'chrome://history/...' variants.
Complete coverage: the instruction has a single requirement (navigate to history page) and the evaluator checks exactly that via URL pattern matching.
